![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226023/assets/97b30cfa241a6e1b9db4d5332749ae503a926711c0e7c78ab188c2327463c89b.png)

Which of the following represents the area enclosed by the first petal of the polar curve $r=3\operatorname{sin}⁡(5\theta ),$ represented by the shaded region shown above?
question.worked_solution:
The area bounded by a polar curve is given by

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{r}^{2}(\theta )\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Since $r(\theta )=3\operatorname{sin}⁡(5\theta )$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{(3\operatorname{sin}⁡(5\theta ))}^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{9}{2}{\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}{sin}^{2}⁡(5\theta )\,\text{d}\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

We now proceed to find the integration limits.  

The curve bounding the region crosses itself at the origin. Therefore, we want to find the values of $\theta $ for which $r=0$, or 

$$
3\operatorname{sin}⁡(5\theta )=0.
$$

This gives us two solutions for $5\theta \in [0,2\pi ):$

$$
5\theta =0,\pi \,⟹\,\theta =0,\frac{\pi }{5}
$$

Therefore, the first petal is traversed for $\theta \in [0,\frac{\pi }{5}].$ Notice that this interval lies in the first quadrant, the same as our petal.

Therefore, our expression for the area is given by

$$
A=\frac{9}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /5}{sin}^{2}⁡(5\theta )\,\text{d}\theta .
$$
